activity.message:
Keep PRIVACY.md and AGENTS.md in line with the data settings

The timetable's Wi-Fi-only rule is its own setting now (Settings > Mobile data), not part of "Save mobile data". The
privacy table also says how often each live feed is asked for.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add a mobile-data screen, a data meter, and stop re-fetching positions whenever a sheet opens

Settings > Live buses > the icon beside "Save mobile data" opens a screen with the data choices and the explanation that
made the old footer too long: how often arrival predictions are fetched on Wi-Fi and on mobile data (automatic, 30 s, 1,
2, 5 minutes, manual), the timetable on Wi-Fi only, and a meter of what the app has downloaded by kind and connection,
with a reset. Bus positions are shown as always live and are not on the list of things that can be slowed.

The vehicle poll lost its place in the cycle every time a sheet opened or the mode changed: it asked at once, usually got
the same feed, and then retried every two seconds for up to eight more 7 KB requests. It now keeps its schedule in the
model and carries on with it; only the foreground, the first start and "refresh now" ask at once. Opening a stop, a bus or
a list fetches fresh predictions by itself (older than 30 s), so the poll no longer has to be restarted for that.

The stop board's rows no longer show a chevron (it pushed the times out of line); "no position yet" already says that a
row has nothing to open.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Make "Later departures" keep working, and keep slow downloads from holding up the positions

"Later departures" showed more only once: the board listed at most 40 departures whatever the window, so at a busy stop the
second tap added nothing. The limit now grows with the window. "Back to now" also scrolls to the top of the list, and
shows next to "Later departures" as well, since it was only offered while earlier departures were open.

The vehicle poll awaited the alerts and the trip predictions (160 KB) before sleeping until the next beat, so a slow
connection delayed the next positions by as long as the predictions took. They now run beside the poll, one at a time.
Live positions are not throttled by any setting except the rider's own "Refresh".

A "poll" log category records how old each new vehicle feed was when it arrived and how many requests it took.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fetch less data, and let the stop board look back and forward

Data: measured with nettop, a stop open cost about 22 MB an hour, because the 160 KB trip updates were fetched with every
30 s beat of the vehicle feed (the "at most once a minute" in the notes was not in the code). They are now fetched at most
every minute (stop, bus, planner, watched route) or two minutes (a focus, a list, the service board), doubled on mobile
data and quadrupled in Low Data Mode while the new "Save mobile data" setting is on, and the 7 MB timetable then waits for
Wi-Fi unless the phone's copy is past its end date. The vehicle poll learns how long after its stamp the city publishes a
feed (PublishLag) instead of asking 1.5 s after and retrying every 2 s; positions and alerts went from 34 to 16 KB a
minute. A stop open now costs about 7 MB an hour.

Stop board: "Earlier departures" (an hour at a time, dimmed, with a "Now" line), "Later departures" and pull-down to go
back to now and refresh. A trip nobody has seen a bus on stays among what is coming for 20 minutes (it was 10) and then
moves to the earlier departures instead of disappearing; a bus that turns up makes it live again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Say where the launchd jobs must live and how to check them after a restart

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep a trip nobody has seen a bus on for ten minutes, marked "No bus seen yet"

A bus has no position until it starts its trip, so a late bus looked as if it had vanished: the trip dropped off a
stop's board the moment its timetable time passed. A trip with no bus (and not cancelled in the trip updates) now stays
for ten minutes, with "No bus seen yet" and how long ago it was due. Ten minutes covers the trips that start late in the
recordings (7% start more than 5 minutes late, 1% more than 10), and a trip that never runs does not linger. The
favourites summary on the service board leaves such trips out.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Pull snapshots in parallel and retry hiccups; say that launchd jobs must live in ~/Library/LaunchAgents

A catch-up after the Mac had been away pulled one snapshot at a time (about an hour per 3,000) and stopped at the first
failed name lookup. Eight requests now run at a time and a dropped connection is retried before giving up.

The README told readers to load the pull job straight from data/launchd/, which is forgotten at the next restart: the
job stopped after the restart of 2026-10-08, and the collector keeps only 6 days, so four days of recordings were lost.
It now says to copy the plist into ~/Library/LaunchAgents first. (It also said two weeks where the collector keeps six
days.)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>

Open a bus on its own destination, keep put-away sheets in a dock, mark estimated positions

- Opening a bus shows the line of its own trip (D2 to Epic Campus or to Verona, not both), and replaces the line another
  bus put on the map, so a bus opened from a stop's board is never hidden by the previous bus's focus.
- Swiping a stop or bus sheet down (or opening the menu) puts it into a dock at the bottom right of the map instead of
  losing it: one chip per bus, stop and journey, stacked; a tap brings the sheet back, the cross lets go of it. The map
  keeps the docked stop or bus marked. This replaces the journey bar.
- A bus drawn ahead of its last report (dead reckoning) has a dashed ring, so an estimate is not mistaken for a fix.
- Rows of a stop's board that can be opened show a chevron; a trip with no bus position says so.
- The live status card and Settings say how often buses report, from a measurement: every bus about every 30 s, 68% of
  single intervals within 25 to 35 s, 4% over 50 s.
- feedanalysis: per-bus report intervals, `early` and `notstarted` commands; findings in docs/data-sources.md.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 Extra <noreply@anthropic.com>
